Npc.Relation: "You stand to inherit some of their dominion, if you prove worthy of their favour"
"You shared a drink, on Mittherbst eve or some other occasion; they expect this tradition to continue."
"You are their secret agent, enacting their will from afar, trusted with things no-one else can know"
"You were once a regular in their court and a trusted advisor, but retired after a very public scandal"
"They claim you are mystically connected to the Eight Winds somehow, so they keep an eye on you"
"You connected them with a powerful sponsor, so they could work magic without fear of persecution"
"You help them to source arcane items that further their understanding of magic"
"Their magic saved you from a horrific fate one Geheimnisnacht or other auspicious occasion"
"They pay you to bring them information, be it local gossip or scrolls from the Great Library of Altdorf"
"They are slowly teaching you everything they know, so you can continue their legacy"
"You trade information transactionally, building your own separate repositories of lore"
"You enjoy debating the finer points of niche trivia that bewilder everyone else"
"You are somehow embroiled in their schemes, be they engaging in forbidden worship, or plotting to replace the Graf of Middenheim"
"You are a trusted spy, rewarded handsomely for the secrets you uncover"
"When you were desperate, their schemes saved you - now you owe them, which makes you useful"
"They are blackmailing you to aid their political agenda, and if you refuse, you will be ruined"
"You're one of their few remaining friends at court - they need your help to get back into high society"
"They're an old friend - you risk your reputation to share a meal on Festag or other occasions"
"You met them after their disgrace, helping to lift them up when they were at their lowest point"
"Their dishonour has tarred you by association, and now you're out in the political wilderness too"
"They ignored your advice and lost a critical battle as a result - a fact you never let them forget"
"They see you as a natural leader, and hope to guide you into a position of command"
"You fought on opposite sides of a war, until they offered you a chance to switch sides"
"You refused to follow their orders, but they spared you the noose"
"You are their trusted deputy, offering counsel and executing their will"
"You saved their life in battle and they have promised to repay the debt"
"You spent many a night together, rank forgotten, perhaps sharing Bugman's best, or Talabec's worst"
"You constantly challenge their authority, but they respect you"
"You worked together once to defeat a common foe"
"They see in you the potential to follow in their footsteps"
"You bonded over your mutual disdain for needless rules and the quibbling of cowardly officers"
"You share stories of triumphs old and new, each of you ever seeking to outdo the other"
"You have followed them in and out of trouble countless times"
"They rescued you, perhaps from the deepest Drakwald or haunted Barren Hills, and never let you forget"
"They tell you spellbinding stories about the wider world, some of which are even true"
"They spotted you doing something incriminating, but have kept quiet for now"
"They recount their harrowing war stories to you, and are glad of your company"
"You respect their deeds, and they respect you in return, helping when they can"
"Orcs, Chaos Marauders, or a rival province's soldiers - you've battled the same foe and bonded over it"
"You've said something to offend them, and you're trying to make it right"
"You fetch them a fresh loaf on Backerstag or other occasions, sharing tales and gossip before you go"
"Their wisdom helps you answer questions you'd never thought to ask before"
"They've been looking out for you as long as you remember, and you're not sure why"
"They tolerate your disrespect because they recognise in you their younger self"
"You have confessed your darkest sins to them, receiving absolution"
"You got up to all sorts of mischief together, before they found their true calling"
"You frequently disagree on spiritual matters, but find the debate stimulating"
"They bless you or your home on Geheimnisnacht, or other occasions when threatened by dark forces"
"They created something for you - a sturdy blade, a finely made ring - and you still owe them for it"
"You've been selling them something, be it good iron, Kemperbad brandy, or simply your own labour"
"They took you on as an apprentice - it didn't work out, but you parted on good terms"
"You accidentally besmirched their work, and are trying to make up for it"
"Be it from a Goblin raid or roaring flames, you saved their establishment and will always be welcome"
"You were once trapped inside their establishment, perhaps by foul weather or besieging Beastmen"
"They need you to help keep their establishment going, otherwise it will sink"
"You still owe them for the problems you caused on your last visit"
"Whatever treatment they gave - a draught of schlafenkraut or a pinch of tarrabeth - it saved your life"
"They provide effective treatment for a persisting ailment."
"They failed to save a loved one, but you know they tried their best"
"They diagnosed you with something incurable - supposedly it will kill you one day"
"You've been following their career for some time, taking inspiration from their adventures"
"You trade information about where opportunities for excitement can be found"
"Your previous work together ended in a double-cross, but neither of you took it personally"
"Perhaps unknowingly, you helped them steal something valuable - Khemrian scrolls, or the Duke's signet ring"
"Their deliveries are the lifeline between you and a distant loved one"
"You're the first person they tell when they learn something scandalous"
"They repeat everything you say far and wide - something you know you can use to your advantage"
"They learned something embarrassing about you and kept it to themselves"
"When you are lost, they offer you guidance, and set you on the right path"
"Every Geheimnisnacht they see a vision of you, and seek to understand its meaning"
"You were friends before you came to understand the powers at their disposal"
"You have fought alongside them, and seen what happens when they get angry"
"They travel the length of the Old World (down the Talabec, or over the Grey Mountains) to find what you need - at a price, of course"
"You tip them off about where to find 'merchandise', in return for favours"
"They stole from you, you stole right back... eventually, you came to an understanding"
"Back in the day, you used to run heists together"
"You sympathise with their heretical creed more than you'd admit in public"
"Their faith is strange to you, but they don't deserve death for it - you shelter them when you can"
"Be they a fanatic of Sigmar, Ahalt the Drinker, or stranger gods still - you believe you can save them"
"They help you because they are convinced one day you will join them... or die"

God.Stricture: "Obey your betters."
"Defend your honour in all matters, and never refuse a challenge."
"Stand honest and true; outside an ambush, trickery and deception are forbidden."
"Only wear pelts from wolves you have slain with weapons crafted by your own hands."
"Black powder, helmets, crossbows, and technology are not Ulric's way."
"Offer a Prayer to Taal for every animal taken."
"Spend a week alone communing with the wilderness each year."
"Eschew metal armour and clad yourself only in the hides of Taal."
"Rely on your own skill, not the advances of gunpowder or cold technology."
"Never harm an animal except in self-defence or for food or sacrifice."
"Defend families, children, and crops from all harm."
"Feel no shame for the flesh Rhya has given you."
"Life is sacred - do no harm unless it is to save another."
"Do not withhold your bounty if you have enough to share."
"Obey your orders."
"Aid Dwarf-folk, never do them harm."
"Promote the unity of the Empire."
"Bear true allegiance to the Imperial throne."
"Show no mercy to Orcs and their kin, the worshippers of dark gods, or to foul witches."
"No whistling or swearing when at sea or on holy ground."
"Never harm an albatross."
"The first catch goes to Manann."
"A silver and fish to every Manannite temple and shrine you pass."
"Hunt down the servants of Stromfels, shark-god and ship-wrecker, wherever they may hide."
"Respect and honour the dead."
"Harm not a raven, for they are fellow servants of Morr."
"Hunt down Necromancers and the Undead wherever they may gather."
"Pay heed to your dreams."
"Never interrupt a funeral service or refuse to conduct one if so ordained."
"At no time be a party to raising the dead unless allowed by Morr."
"One coin in 10 belongs to Ranald."
"Never betray another to the authorities: there is no greater sin than informing."
"Violence is prohibited except in self-defence."
"It is better to live free and die than endure under oppression."
"There is no honour among thieves, but there is among Ranaldans."
"Never refuse to arbitrate a dispute when asked."
"Always tell the truth without fear or favour."
"Protect knowledge at all costs."
"Combat must be a last resort when all other approaches prove fruitless."
"Never become a tool of injustice or heresy."
"Act with honour and dignity in all matters."
"Respect prisoners of war, and never kill a foe who surrenders."
"Show no mercy to unrepentant enemies of Humanity."
"Obey all honourable orders."
"Preserve the weak from the horrors of war."
"Render assistance without judgment, based only on need."
"Never kill except in self-defence or when facing followers of the Fly Lord."
"Hunt down those who swear themselves to gods of suffering and decay."
"Shallya's work is never done, so turn not to self-indulgence."
"Never take up arms; a walking stick and courage will suffice."

DATA_MISCAST.Row: "All those within Medium Range feel a sudden sense of loss, though they cannot say exactly what they have misplaced."
"A sickly wave of magic escapes your grasp. Anyone within Short Range of you feels a sudden sense of nausea, but there is no other effect."
"1d10 random small objects within Short Range are transfigured into various small creatures which scuttle away in random directions."
"A hideous chittering is heard from a nearby shadow. Until Mannslieb next hangs full in the sky, you continue to hear this disturbing noise at frequent but entirely unpredictable intervals."
"All fresh food within Long Range is spoiled. Dried, salted, pickled, or otherwise preserved food remains palatable."
"Arcane power spills forth from you in every direction. You are Staggered, and a minor effect associated with a Lore you know occurs within Short Range of you."
"A hideous stench erupts from you. All those within Short Range must immediately Give Ground or suffer a -1d penalty to their next Test. All your Fellowship Tests are Grim until you can next bathe."
"The weather changes suddenly and unnaturally in the local area, with malefic storms appearing out of clear skies, or frigid snows falling in the middle of Sommerzeit."
"You are suddenly transported to a random Zone within Medium Range of your current location."

"Your eyes become blind to the good light of the sun, and you can only see by torchlight or other artificial or arcane illumination, as though it were the dead of night. This lasts until your next downtime."
"An unnatural wind whips up around you. Anyone within Short Range, including you, falls Prone unless they are a Monstrosity."
"A random spell you have recently cast is immediately cast again with a Potency of 1. The target of this spell is decided by the GM. (Printed range 22-23 in the book.)"
"The Winds of Magic twist your tongue, robbing you of the ability to tell a lie. Until your next downtime, you may only speak the truth as you understand it."

"Your eyes are overwhelmed by stray arcane energies. Until Morrslieb next hangs full in the sky, you can perceive only the Winds of Magic, not the natural world. Most normal Awareness Tests become Grim for you, but all Tests to detect magical phenomena are Glorious instead."

"Magic surrounds you, wreathing you in an illusion drawn from the deepest recesses of your mind. You take on the appearance of whatever foe you most fear. This lasts until the end of the battle, or for the next few minutes."
"Magic rips through your body, causing a great deal of internal damage. You immediately suffer a Wound: roll on the Wound Table, adding any additional dice for existing Wounds as normal."

"The Winds of Magic swirl around you. Your current Zone becomes a Hazard until the end of the current Battle, with a rating equal to the number of Miscast dice you rolled. Those in the Zone may resist its effects with either Endurance or Athletics."

"An unnatural screech erupts from your lips, audible for miles around. You and anyone within Short Range suffer a Wound: specifically, the 'Ears ringing' Wound (result 11 on the Wounds table, page 190)."

"You open a rift in reality that leads to the Realm of Chaos, and a Daemon erupts forth, entirely hostile, seeking to beguile, corrupt or destroy the caster and their allies. The GM may use any stat block from the Gamemaster's Guide. It may act immediately or flee, biding its time. The entity returns to the Realm of Chaos when it, or the caster, are destroyed."

"You open a rift in reality that leads to the Realm of Chaos, in a Zone of the GM's choosing within Long Range. Those who witness it must pass a Difficult (-1d) Willpower Test or become fascinated and be drawn to enter the rift unless restrained. The rift closes only once someone has entered it, or something has emerged."

"Magic overcomes you in a spectacular miasma of unnatural energy, ripping your body apart and spreading it over every Zone within Medium Range. You are dead, your body beyond salvation or reanimation."

Career.Note: "The printed Trappings cell ends with 'and either' with nothing after it (book truncation). Check the printed book or errata."
"The Skill Bonuses line of the PDF reads '1 to four' without the plus sign (typo); '+1 to four' as on the other careers. Trade tools: 'to match your Trade Lore'. The Trade Lore is 'custom' (p.88)."
"Lore 'Waterways' = the book writes 'Riverways' on the career sheets (see TOW_DONNEES.md, spelling to unify at the lore batch)."
"Trappings 'Axe or sword, axe or shield' is printed that way (two slots, the second offers axe or shield)."
"Last trappings slot: 'hunting kit or trade tools to match your Trade Lore (if applicable)'. The Labourer sheet writes 'Waterways' where Boathand writes 'Riverways' (lore spelling to unify)."
"Lore slot 1 = the Cult Lore of your god, slot 2 = your god's Favoured Lore (chapter 7, to be linked at the gods batch)."
"Skill Bonuses line printed '+1 to any four of the following' (same meaning as the other careers). 'two pistols' = quantity 2."

"Lore slot 1 = 'Troll Slayer or other Monster Slayer Lore (choose one)', slot 2 = 'Mountaineering or other Environment Lore (choose one)'. Trappings 'Axe, greataxe or second axe': the second slot offers greataxe or a second axe."
"Skill Bonuses line printed '+1 four of the following' (missing 'to'), read as the usual +1 to four."
